The two young men were swept away in the currents. When they came back to themselves they saw that they were lying on a beautiful piece of land near a village. "What do we do now?" said one to the other. "We'll go and see the Chief of the Village," said the other. "But how are we going to find the Chief of the Village?" said one. "We'll go and ask the people," said the other.
So they went to ask the people where the Chief of the Village was. "The Chief of the Village is in the middle of the village," said one. "But how are we going to find the middle of the village?" said the other. "Ask the people," said one. "What do you mean, 'ask the people'?" said the other. "There are too many people and too many houses. How are we going to find the Chief of the Village?" Just then a little girl came up and said, "The Chief of the Village is in the largest long house at the center of the village."

But one of the two young men had seen the Chief of the Harbour and now he was very afraid. "Why are you afraid?" said the Chief of the Harbour. "I am the Chief of the Harbour and I save people from the water." "Then why did you come to our village?" "I came to your village to marry one of your daughters." At this the young men laughed. "You are old," they said. "You are the Chief of the Harbour and you are old." The Chief of the Harbour went away laughing to himself. And that is the story of the Chief of the Harbour.
